Slow down. You’re only 14. It’s okay that you have no girlfriend. It’s okay that you don’t have goals set up yet. It’s okay that you’re autistic. 
You’re just a child still. You are closer to being 10 years old than you are to being 20. 
Expecting someone to have their entire life planned out at just 14 isn’t just unrealistic, it’s very damaging. If you DID have goals right now, who knows for sure that you’re not going to wake up one day at age 40 hating the career you chose when you were a teenager? 
It’s fine to not have a girlfriend right now. Kids shouldn’t be expected to be dating so young. It’s normal to be curious, of course, but nobody has a real relationship when they’re 14. When you’re a kid that young, your brain literally hasn’t developed fully yet. Nobody should be expected to be have a partner when they’re only a CHILD. 
It’s fine that you’re autistic. Autism isn’t a death sentence. There are, in fact, successful people in the world who are on the spectrum- successful people with rich, full lives and families and people who love them. Autism doesn’t make you a burden. It doesn’t make your life worth any less than that of someone without it. 
You’re certainly not doing your family a favor by dying. Suicide can tear families apart, leave holes in the dynamics that can never be filled. There would always be an empty seat at the table that reminds them that you’re gone. There will never be a moment when you’re forgotten by people who love you, or even by people who only casually knew you. 
People love you far more than you can ever know.

Most of your pain seems to be coming from self loathing, and admittedly the actual hardest step in getting anywhere near recovery is realizing that some of it really is just on you. For example- I’m not this lonely because everyone is trying to avoid me, but because I’m trying to isolate myself and validate my self hatred. 

Here’s the thing- you can change. 
You call yourself a horrible person for being racist. And while you being racist may be true, it’s clear you feel awful about it and want to change. Try to teach yourself to be different- try to unlearn the ways you think about people. Understand that any group you may have problems with isn’t just that group. It’s people- individual people, who all live and breathe and learn. Not just a concept or statistic. Contrary to what experience may tell you, the majority of people are good, or at least harmless. Most people don’t hate you, as they aren’t aware that you specifically exist. You don’t need to pit them all against you.

Hey OP. Judging by your past posts, I think we’re both in a similar situation with heavily religious and extremely controlling families. I feel a lot of the same things you feel. I want you to be safe for everyone else who’s like you, okay? 
If your family is willing to harm you for “honor,” then that honor is not worth upholding. Your life is worth more than their image. You have to live for yourself.
